title: T-3121: limit automatic full-smoke measurements to DEV
body:
A feature branch that merges DEV after a full-smoke workflow edit starts another unfiltered measurement. Those runs reach the 150-minute limit and prevent otherwise green PRs from merging (#1277 and #1278).

Restrict the workflow’s automatic own-file push self-test to `dev`. Branch and path filters both apply. Automatic measurements also stop on `main` and tags; explicit dispatch, the nightly bake’s smoke, both viewport defaults, all 15 parts, the 150-minute measurement limit and every renderer assertion remain unchanged. This changes one workflow file and no merge-policy code.

This is an invisible CI repair that unblocks the visible work in #1277/#1278. T-3121’s integration acceptance still requires those PRs to merge through ordinary green checks without a blind override.

Validation:

- Full preflight: **1,064 steps / 384 self-tests**, none red, 673.643s. Cleanup reaped 721 owned descendants with none remaining. Committed tree `534ff7c9` equals the validated input.
- Seven trigger/YAML cases passed; the only semantic change is `push.branches: [dev]`.
- App/reference content is identical to accepted DEV `33a99a55`. Existing exact-source renderer evidence and the inherited release-note fold are being checked separately; the focused published news probe and fresh normal PR CI are pending. No new whole-renderer pass is claimed by the static test.

This owner-visible PR remains draft while those final checks run.

title: T-3105, T-3119, T-3120: First-fort galleries and reliable 1812 plantings
body:
Five first-fort ranges gain two-storey courtyard galleries, source-shaped openings and chimney counts. Their upper beams meet the existing canopy, closing the reviewed 30–58 mm gap without moving roofs, posts or footprints. Two blockhouses lose invented domestic chimneys. Metric dimensions, glazing and hidden features remain reconstructed or unresolved.

This group owns T-3105 (fort ranges), T-3119 (four Kinzie poplars and six Ouilmette currants with clearance) and T-3120 (1812 Light/Full woodland reach within unchanged caps). It has one What's-New entry with three items. Original T-2387/T-3041 remain open: all sixteen earlier and eight new same-camera comparisons still **DIFFERS**.

Hogan PR [#1283](https://github.com/kevinrhaas/chicago/pull/1283) is now merged into `dev`. This branch integrates its actual squash and automatic changelog fold. Six ancestry conflicts were resolved only after proving each incoming blob equals the Hogan source already integrated here. Against full-smoke-tested `308b738e`, the resolved tree changes exactly two automatic changelog-fold paths; every other blob is identical. The already-folded pending Hogan entry was removed after exact title/kind/items equality checks.

Validation:

- Genuine pinned Blender 4.5.3 exports and real web derivatives for all 25 fort-family models. Seven initial targets change; 18 defaults preserve physical geometry, normals, materials and confidence. The beam correction changes five beam regions; the other 20 model/web assets remain exact. Independent decoding verifies roof contact and no coplanar timber top; maximum web residual is 0.304 mm, within measured quantisation bounds.
- Native rebuild/population checks pass. All 26 protected population/policy files and 105 log/frame recipe sets remain exact to the upstream; independent Hogan preservation checks pass.
- Fourteen standard mobile/desktop app cases pass, with all 56 states directly reviewed. An additional actual published Fly inspection shows supported courtyard galleries. It establishes no on-foot access; the existing grounded courtyard failure remains recorded.
- **All 18 published smoke parts pass on `308b738e`: 829 desktop and 836 mobile assertions, zero failures or page errors.** Full 1904 measures 4,191 calls / 3,943,402 triangles against unchanged 7,800 / 4.6M caps; Light remains within its own caps.
- The resolved current-`dev` tree independently passes **1,065 check steps, including 384 self-tests**, with required readers and unchanged source. Its only served delta is the automatic Hogan release entry. Actual published mobile/desktop checks repeat the original unread/returning-visitor assertions and verify the folded entry exactly once, its exact text and no page overflow. This is targeted changed-data verification; the all-18 result above belongs to `308b738e`.

Roof proportions, materials, stack placement, cameras, context and the magazine-identification erratum remain open. The release-feed probe also records text extending beyond the inner panel at both sizes; its no-page-overflow result does not establish a clipping-free feed. No renderer CSS changes are included here. This bounded increment does not complete an original picture-match ticket.

[Recovery index and full-18 evidence](https://github.com/kevinrhaas/chicago-evidence/blob/169121784700e7d5a0d06b02639831dd7bacb4ef/evidence/image-match-2026-10-23/resumed-20261023T2245/RECOVERY.md). The reconciliation and actual delivery receipts are checkpointed in the same evidence repository.

title: T-3113: 1812 Prairie's balcony and projection top to the Levy photograph
body:
## T-3113 — 1812 Prairie's balcony and projection top to the Levy photograph

Piece 1 of T-3092, which this run split (`T-3114` keeps the entrance arch, transom, fanlight and stair: the elliptical head needs K06's shared `Head`, and the jamb on the projection's corner needs K08 or K07 geometry of its own).

**What.** The south projection's balcony is now built the way Albert Levy's print shows its front run:
- a stone panel 3.14 m across (x 390-680 px), 0.09 m high at its ends, sweeping straight up over 0.8 m to 0.42 m shoulders, then level to a pedestal 0.32 m across and 0.52 m high, under a cap that sits at about the rail's top (x 527-557 px);
- an iron scroll hung from the rail over each sweep, and a carved scroll on the panel beside the pedestal;
- the top rail runs into the pedestal, and the foot rail stops at the panel's ends;
- a roundel under the rail on every baluster.

The projection's top comes down to the print's cornice. Its last storey is now 3.65 m, so the wall head stands at 9.25 m under a 0.2 m × 0.15 m eave whose top is at 9.40 m. Before, K08's 0.35/0.28 m eave over 9.45 m put the top at 9.73 m, about 25-30 px over the print's cornice. K08's balcony learns `panel` and `roundel`, both validated in `k01_frontage_params`. All 24 other K01 houses re-emit byte-identical; only their manifest input hashes move.

**Records.** Levy items 15 and 16 and c. 1955 item 11 are now `fixed`. Two new open Levy items: the stone frieze under the cornice (built in brick), and the cornice's moulded section. The liberty is `L-k08-1812-balcony-panel-3113`. It records what is invented: the panel's thickness, the scroll form, and the 0.07 m scroll radius against the print's about 0.11 m.

**Verification.**
- `tools/check.sh`: **CHECK PASS**, 1063 steps, none red. Along the way it caught two coplanar overlaps in K08 (the pedestal's bed, the scroll's core), and both are fixed. numpy appears only in tagged self-test lines.
- Smoke legs (`--for-diff` names parts 1-15, because the mesh moved):
  - desktop 3: 107/107 pass;
  - mobile 3: 107/107 pass;
  - desktop 14: killed by the 590 s foreground cap (dev's own reading of that part is 29 min), not a verdict;
  - desktop 1: killed by the cap at load 4.4 after 65 passes and no failure, not a verdict.
- Photo match: both views re-rendered on the final GLB. The balcony and the cornice read within a few px of the print through the Levy camera.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


### Continuation status — 24 October 2026

This PR is draft while T-3113’s owned balcony/photo discrepancy is corrected and verified. The existing public-domain Levy comparison still records a roughly 0.11m scroll against the 0.07m model and a placement difference. An isolated, uncommitted source candidate addresses that discrepancy; emitted geometry, support, normals and deliberate rejection controls are under independent review. No new source commit or branch push is claimed.

The current DEV integration also has two generated conflicts awaiting their canonical owner rebuild. Ordered derivation, current photo renders and complete gates remain pending. T-3113’s blank acceptance template and missing image-gate section are not a photo-acceptance waiver. The existing `differs` records and broader Wheeler photo work remain open; no view has been marked `matches` by this continuation.


### Saved correction and overlapping continuation

The remote head subsequently advanced to `a1f8176e`, merging DEV `de91c45b` into `cb0d1166`. The separate scroll correction is not in that head: Wheeler’s scroll data and K08 source, photos, cameras and match verdicts remain unchanged from `cb0d1166`.

The exact uncommitted correction is available in [checkpoint 23](https://github.com/kevinrhaas/chicago-evidence/tree/61af27896b2efcbe34a230d3c5cf95032607e67a/evidence/transport-recovery-2026-10-24/CHECKPOINT-23-PR1281-UNCOMMITTED-PHOTO-CORRECTION-WIP), including source/conflict snapshots, provenance and the independent review’s corrected geometry. One bounded emitted-geometry proof passed in 0.392s: six deliberate corruptions rejected and 1,424 triangle normals checked, with complete cleanup. This is local construction evidence only; exported GLB, current photo evidence and complete qualification remain pending. No view has been marked `matches` and no scroll candidate commit or push was made by this continuation. The isolated WIP is frozen to avoid duplicate writes while the other continuation proceeds.

title: T-3107: 1801 Prairie's south face from HABS photograph 1, and its two stone stacks
body:
## T-3107 — 1801 Prairie's south face from HABS photograph 1, and its two stone stacks

Piece 1 of 4 of T-3003, which was split this run (T-3108, T-3109 and T-3110 hold the rest).

**What shipped**
- **The picture.** HABS IL-1077 photograph 1 (Harold Allen, June 1965, from the south-west), the only known picture of the Kimball house's south side. Taken from the LOC master TIFF (5292 px), committed as an 1800 px copy at `chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/public/kimball-habs-photo-01.jpg`, with source record `habs_kimball_photo_01_sw_1965`. Not mirrored: the NO PARKING sign reads true.
- **The camera**: `data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/habs_1965_01_southwest.json`. The eye is raised about 7.7 m over the west side of Prairie Avenue, rolled -0.93° (the plate is turned), f 1778 px. It fits the loggia arch, the south wall's full run to the south-east corner, the first south window column and the south bay's window to within about 10 px. **It does not fit the south cornice at the south-west corner**, where the render sits about 85 px below the print. The solve says so and leaves it to T-3108, because the front that would settle it is the part T-3108 rebuilds. The print also shows that the pavilion is narrower than built, with a two-storey round bay between it and the south wall.
- **The match record**: verdict `differs`, 1 fixed, 13 open, 3 not shown. Each open item names the piece that owns it.
- **The two south stacks.** One small reconstructed brick stack is replaced by two tall stacks in the walls' stone, both rising from the cornice over the wall line: one at u 14.45 (about 1.2 m across), one at u 3.2 (about 1.45 m, cap at about 20.1 m). This needed a new per-stack `fabric: "stone"` in the K01 kit. It is additive: no other house uses it, and every other K01/K12/K13/K16 mesh re-emits byte-identical (they were only marked stale by the generator edit).
- **The height ruling.** In the 1965 print the front stack stands about 3.5 m over the cresting beside it, but the c. 1895 Taylor print shows only sky there. The phase guard prefers the period view, so the front stack is built to 18.0 m, the most Taylor allows. The conflict is open in both match records and in `L-kimball-1801-south-stacks-3107`.
- The Taylor match record was re-read against the new GLB (verdict `differs` restored, plus one `not shown` item for the stacks). Also: the liberty entry and a What's-New entry (`changelog.d/T-3107.json`).

**Verification**
- `./tools/check.sh`: 1062 of 1063 steps passed. The one failure was the derived built-so-far walk; I regenerated it, and `jaunt_built_so_far.py --check` and `compile_scene.py --all --check` both pass on the committed tree.
- `validate.py --stale`: PASS (0 errors).
- Smoke, `--published`, desktop:
  - part 3: **SMOKE PASS** (107 checks).
  - part 1: 91 checks passed, including zero page errors, and no failing check. My own 590 s cap cut it short before the end, so it did not finish (the runner is slow today).
- The pieces left open: T-3108 (south-west round bay, pavilion, camera re-solve), T-3109 (south bay, openings, dormers, stack heads, south-east pinnacle), T-3110 (east side and rear from HABS 2).

title: T-3111: 1811 Prairie's north pier, from the 1888 plate, the Chicagology photograph and the 1965 HABS photograph
body:
## T-3111: 1811 Prairie's 1965 HABS photograph, and the front's north pier it shows

T-3111 is piece 1 of T-3101, which this run split. T-3101's last clause, "every 1811 match record brought to matches", needs more than one run: the south flank waits on T-3099, and the pier's own cap needs kit work. That clause is now **T-3112**, beside it in the queue.

**Acceptance (stated before work):** the HABS photograph's camera solved into `data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/`, with its residuals stated and checked on something it was not fitted to. Its match record written element by element. The Building Budget sketch kept to its phase guard, with the reason written down. Whatever the picture shows of 1811 that the build gets wrong, fixed where the kit can do it.

### The HABS photograph (`habs_1965.json`)
- Harold Allen's June 1965 photograph (HABS IL-1077, Library of Congress, no known restrictions) is a picture **of 1801**, looking across the court. It sees 1811 only at its right edge, x 927–983 px.
- Its camera is fitted to 1801 in 1811's frame, by least squares on 7 readings. The 1801 render is shown as context.
  - Residuals: 0.4–4.0 px, plus 5.8 px (weighted) on the north end's height.
- **Checked on readings it was not fitted to:**
  - The pier's south edge, as the 1888 plate reads it, lands at x 970. The print's downpipe at that junction stands at x 972–975.
  - 1801's entrance arch lands about 15 px off, which is within what 1801's own build is good to.
- **Not good for 1811 heights.** Its vertical scale is 1801's, carried 14 m across the court. The solve says so.

### Visible: the north pier
- All three pictures show the front's north end as a **pier of rock-faced brownstone about 0.93 m wide**, standing between the north arris and the bay's canted cheek:
  - the 1888 plate at x 52–92 px;
  - the Chicagology photograph at x 110–185 px;
  - the HABS photograph at x 927–972 px.
- The build started the cheek 0.3 m from the corner, which hid most of the pier. The strip that was left showed as plain pale trim.
  - Earlier reads put the canted face at plate x 60–112, and the Chicagology solve put its north end at x 134. Both of those points are in the middle of the pier.
  - The 1911 sheet's trace (about 0.16 m) cannot settle this. At the sheet's 50 ft scale, 0.77 m is about a millimetre.
- **Fix:** `cant_left_m` 1.99 → 1.36, so the cheek now leaves the wall at v 0.93. The front's north corner (v 2.29) has not moved. The bay's window `at` fractions were re-derived for the new girth, so every light keeps its place.
- **Generator:** K01 drew one seat box round a whole bay. The bay's cornice reaches the wall at v 0.37, so that box stripped the coursing off the bare pier below it. A bay with a **canted** cheek now seats its walls separately from its cornice and deck.
  - The change is gated on a `canted` flag. Only 1811 has a cant, so no other house's geometry moves.
- **Result:** the pier now renders at x 51–92 on the plate, 113–190 on the Chicagology print and 928–970 on the HABS print, in rock-faced courses.
- Rebuilt with `k01_emit`. `k01_frontage.py`'s bytes are hashed into every K01 mesh's inputs, so the 31 K01-hashed assets were re-emitted. Their meshes are **byte-identical** (`k01_emit --check`); only the recorded `inputs_sha256` in the manifest moved.

### Match records
- All four records are re-read, with verdict `differs`.
- New open items, now owned by T-3112:
  - the pier's own cap, which stands 0.3–0.5 m under the bay's cornice with a small slate top;
  - the string course the build runs across the pier;
  - the downpipe at the pier's junction with the cheek.
- The Chicagology record's "north eave" item now says that the "cornice returning at x 115–135 px" is the pier's cap.

### Building Budget sketch (phase guard kept)
- The caption's house number is not legible ("18?9").
- It draws a four-arch open loggia with a stair rising *along* the front. 1811's own pictures show one deep arch with a straight stair square to the front.
- So it gets no camera under 1811. The reason is in the assets README.

### Verification
- `check.sh` whole: **did not finish**. It ran to the 590 s cap (rc 124) with no failed step in its transcript. Every gate step covering this diff was then run on its own, on the rebased tree, and all are green:
  - `validate.py --all` and `--stale`: PASS, 0 stale;
  - `k01_emit --check`;
  - `compile_scene --all --check`;
  - `compile_liberties --check`;
  - `image_gate --check` and `--test`;
  - `changelog-entries --check`;
  - `k01_contract --check`;
  - `test_k01_round_corner`, `test_k01_tower`, `test_k01_pavilion_past_eave`, `test_k01_side_read_windows`, `test_k01_wing_past_host`;
  - `test_frontage_faces`, `check_frontage_notes`, `measure_frontage_declaration`.
- After rebasing onto dev (T-3096's Glessner rebake), this clone's untracked Glessner v4 copies were re-materialised from dev's archive (`recover_glessner_v4.py --materialize`). `--stale` then passes.
- Smoke on the published mirror:
  - desktop part 1 (scaffold): 95/95 PASS;
  - desktop part 3 (the card and citations): 107/107 PASS;
  - mobile part 3: 107/107 PASS.
- CI's `chicago-4d-check` is the full gate, and the merge waits on it.

Visible-progress: **visible**. 1811's north corner now stands as a rock-faced stone pier.

title: T-3013: the 1904 state of sheet 35w's five Indiana-side lots; Bane Brothers' livery at 2129 drafted
body:
## T-3013: the 1904 state of sheet 35w's five Indiana-side lots

T-3009 left four lots (2001-2003, 2101-2105, 2129-2131 Indiana and 215-217 E. 21st, plus the open lot beside 215) `phase_unresolved`: the 1911 atlas shows them in 1911 commercial use, and nothing on hand said what stood there on 1 July 1904. This PR reads them from dated sources found through the Internet Archive's full-text search.

### What the sources say (12 new source records, all public domain)
| lot | 1904 reading | sources | ruling |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2001-2003 Indiana | 2001 a residence (A. Courtney Campbell and Mrs. George C. Morton, **Blue Book 1904**; still a private family's house in 1907 and taking boarders in Sept 1909). 2003 a 12-room stone-front house to let in 1902 | Blue Book 1904, Lakeside 1902, Tribune 1902-10-17 / 1907-10-04 / 1909-09-14 | `replaced_after_1904`: the 1911 printing works is later. Nothing is drawn yet because the houses' outline isn't known |
| 2101-2105 Indiana | an agent's office at 2105 from Jan 1904; furnished rooms at 2101 in 1905-07; the Stanley Motor Carriage Co. only by Apr 1909 | Tribune 1904-01-31 / 1905-06-05 / 1909-04-02 | `replaced_after_1904`, nothing drawn |
| 215-217 E. 21st | a furnished room to let at 215, 23 July 1904; Security Demountable Rim Co. by 1910 | Tribune 1904-07-23 | `replaced_after_1904`, nothing drawn |
| 2129-2131 Indiana | **Bane Brothers' livery and boarding stables, "2125, 2127 and 2129 Indiana Ave."** (Blue Book 1904; Lakeside 1902); 2123-2129 in 1905; G. G. West's livery 1910; West Motor Livery Co. garage 2127-2129 in 1911 on the same 405/406 lines | Blue Books 1904, 1905, 1910, 1911; Lakeside 1902 | `present_as_mapped` (inferred) and **drafted**: `livery_2129_indiana`, beside the 2123 livery |
| open lot W of 215 | nothing legible found | — | stays `phase_unresolved`; the census now records that it was searched |
| 2133 Indiana (not traced) | Louis Rueckert's corner saloon in both the 1902 and 1911 Lakeside directories; households at 202-210 E. 22nd in 1902 | Lakeside 1902 | recorded in the census `_doc` only |

The 1890s Sanborn volumes on LoC don't cover vol. 3's area, and the 1904 Lakeside directory isn't on the Internet Archive. LoC and HathiTrust were behind Cloudflare challenges from this runner.

### Changes
- `edges_census_s35w.json`: rulings, a `reading_1904` (text + source ids) on each row, and the 2129 polygon is now `non_building_use` like 2123's livery.
- `trace_prairie_1904_footprints.py`: the new `replaced_after_1904` ruling is read as `not_1904`. The trace re-derives, and only s35w moves.
- `draft_prairie_1904.json` and `.py`: the 2129 livery frontage row. A drafted `use` can now cite its own sources (`use.sources`), and only this record uses that. The skip reasons are rewritten for the three replaced lots.
- Bake `--only livery_2129_indiana` (GLB + web derivative + sidecar).
- New liberty `L-draft-livery-2129-3013`; L264's brick population restated 159 → 160.
- Re-derived: generator-half asset count 968 → 969, source use, the closing research audit, land tracts.
- `compile_source_use.py` INDEX_BUDGET 168 000 → 176 000. The 12 sources took the raw index to 168 436 bytes, and this follows the documented ~8 KB-step precedent. The 120 KB compressed first-open allowance is unchanged.
- `smoke_renderer.mjs`: stage 14's PLACED_1904 now names `livery_2129_indiana`. This avoids the omission T-3057 had to repair after T-3009.
- What's New: `changelog.d/T-3013.json`.

### Verification
- `tools/check.sh` doesn't fit one 600 s foreground call on this runner: it reached 500 of ~1,049 steps at 585 s. So I ran its steps in three numbered ranges under check.sh's own harness (a wrapper that sources `check_harness.sh` and counts `step`/`selftest` calls). The result was **CHECK PASS on all three: 300 + 260 + 489 steps, none red**, on the final tree, with numpy/scipy installed so no step stood on a banked reading.
- `node tools/changelog-entries.mjs --check`: OK.
- Smoke: `--for-diff` names every part (new mesh and manifest). Desktop stage 14, the leg that asserts the 1904 placed set, could not finish under the 590 s cap: 72 s to ready, then killed mid-stage. Every check it reached passed, including "every structure that should draw, drew" and "zero page errors". The only FAIL line, "the suite body ran to completion", is the browser closing when the timeout killed the run.
- Checked stage 14's assertion directly instead: the smoke's PLACED_1904 list equals the 1904 scene index's structure set exactly (223 = 223, `livery_2129_indiana` in both).

### Follow-up
A new ticket covers outlines for the 1904 buildings at 2001-2003, 2101-2105 and 215 E. 21st: a pre-1909 plate (Robinson 1886 vol. 1 south of 20th, Rascher), a permit or a photograph. It also covers the open lot west of 215.
